messages:
anna: Quick Q — planning a tiny canary change, want a sanity check before I push the TF PR. We need to route ~5% traffic to a canary pod pool and use NodePort so NLB passthrough can healthcheck the pod directly. Thinking of switching svc from ClusterIP -> NodePort and set externalTrafficPolicy: Local so client IP is preserved. Any obvious pitfalls?

anna: current svc snippet i want to change:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
  namespace: inference
spec:
  type: ClusterIP # current
  selector:
    app: inference
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
```

anna: target change (in tf manifest):
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference" {
  metadata { name = "inference-svc" namespace = "inference" }
  spec {
    type = "NodePort"
    selector = { app = "inference" }
    port { port = 80 target_port = 8080 name = "http" }
    external_traffic_policy = "Local"
  }
}
```

anna: also we have a legacy health check that expects nodePort 32080 to be open from the NLB. If we switch, TF will allocate a random nodePort unless we pin it. Questions:
- pin nodePort vs let k8s allocate? (pinning requires tf to know port in all clusters)
- externalTrafficPolicy Local -> will break pod distribution during rolling updates?
- probe binding: our Gateway API TCPRoute expects the NLB to probe the NodePort. Any gotchas with TLS passthrough cert secretbinding (cross-namespace) when service is NodePort?

devin: Short answers first: pin if your healthcheck config can't be changed quickly. Local preserves client IP but means traffic only goes to nodes with pods -> possible uneven distribution if pods not on all nodes.

kyu: Also watch connection tracking. NodePort + externalTrafficPolicy:Local with high RPS can cause per-node imbalance. For canary 5% probably fine but if you scale down pods to 1 per node you'll get hot nodes.

sam: Re: probe & TLS passthrough — NodePort doesn't change secretbinding behavior because TLS passthrough terminates at pods (or at the app) if you're not doing TLS termination at the LB. But if you rely on Gateway API TLS termination (Gateway does TLS) then NLB probes will need to hit the Gateway listener target (different flow). Which are you using?

anna: We use Gateway API with passthrough (we bind TLS secret via SecretBinding to the gateway namespace) — so the NLB is in passthrough mode, it forwards TCP to NodePort. The Gateway routes to the service via TCPRoute. So TLS is terminated by the pod.

devin: OK that means NodePort + Local is fine RULE-WISE. A few practical tips:
- pin nodePort to the legacy probe (set it in TF) so the NLB health check keeps working during rollout.
- make a rollout plan: create canary svc with node selector for canary nodes or use label + traffic-shift at Gateway so you can move 5% without changing global svc for main.
- add readiness probe that responds on health endpoint on 8080 so NLB health is consistent.

anna: quick terraform detail: if i pin nodePort in TF and later change cluster autoscaling, will TF complain if the nodePort conflicts?

kyu: TF will complain only if there is already a Service with that nodePort in the cluster. Port reuse across namespaces is allowed on different nodeports? Actually nodePorts are cluster-scoped, so if another service already uses that nodePort you'll get API error. Use a port range that our infra reserves (check infra docs).

infra-bot: FYI — reserved nodePort ranges for prod clusters: 32000-32767. Non-prod: 31000-31999. See docs: https://redwood-infra/docs/nodeport-policy

sam: Also add a short-lived canary: create a separate Service inference-svc-canary that is NodePort pinned and update Gateway TCPRoute to point 5% of weight to that backend. That avoids mutating the main service runtime.

anna: sweet. final checklist before i open PR:
- [ ] pin nodePort to 32080 in TF
- [ ] set externalTrafficPolicy: Local
- [ ] add/update readiness probe on pods (8080/health)
- [ ] make inference-svc-canary + Gateway weight change for 5%
- [ ] run terraform plan in staging cluster and validate no port collisions
- [ ] @devin for review, @kyu for perf/numbers, @sam for Gateway routing review

devin: ACK will review once you drop PR link. Also add note in PR about rollback (how to remove NodePort if it flares).

kyu: I'll check perf impact with a quick load test once canary is up. If you need a perf script ping me.

sam: Ping me when you update TCPRoute YAML. Quick glance after PR. :thumbsup:

anna: Thanks all — i'll implement and link PR here in ~30m.

anna: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3124 (contains TF change + k8s svc fragment + Gateway TCPRoute update). Please review!

devin: Looking. small nit: make the nodePort value a variable with allowed list fallback to reserved range.

sam: LGTM overall, one comment about adding a changelog entry for the NLB healthcheck mapping so oncall knows the nodePort.

kyu: perf test script attached in PR comments. running a short 60s ramp now.

devin: Approved, left one tf fmt nit.

sam: Approved from gateway side.

anna: rolling canary now, will monitor. thanks everyone :party-parrot:
